layers.name: Sources
layers.plain_blurb: Straight from Stripe, the CRM, the website. Nobody has cleaned it yet.

entities.name: raw.stripe.charges
entities.description: Raw Stripe charge events, landed by Fivetran every 15 minutes.
entities.plain_description: Every payment a customer has made — how much, in what currency, and whether it went through.
entities.why: Every revenue number in the company is built from this.

entities.name: raw.events.checkout_events
entities.plain_description: What people clicked on their way through the checkout.
entities.why: Shows where people give up before paying.

entities.name: raw.crm.customers
entities.description: Customer records synced from the CRM.
entities.plain_description: Who our customers are, when they signed up, and what plan they're on.
entities.why: Nothing about a customer can be worked out without it.

entities.name: raw.stripe.refunds
entities.description: Raw Stripe refund events. Netted off revenue in fct_orders.
entities.plain_description: Money we've handed back to customers.
entities.why: Revenue is wrong if refunds aren't subtracted.

entities.name: raw.support.tickets
entities.description: Support tickets from Zendesk. Ticket volume is a churn signal.
entities.plain_description: Complaints and questions customers have raised.
entities.why: People who complain a lot are often about to leave.

layers.name: Modelled
layers.plain_blurb: The raw data tidied and combined into things people can actually use.

entities.name: analytics.core.dim_customer
entities.plain_description: The customer list, cleaned up and standardised.

entities.name: analytics.core.fct_orders
entities.description: One row per completed order, with revenue in USD.
entities.plain_description: One row per completed order, with the money converted into dollars.
entities.why: This is where 'how much did we make' gets answered.

entities.name: analytics.marts.customer_ltv
entities.plain_description: How much money each customer has brought in over the last year.
entities.why: Used to decide who's worth keeping and how hard to try.

entities.name: analytics.features.customer_features
entities.plain_name: The numbers the AI learns from
entities.description: Feature table serving the churn and LTV models.
entities.plain_description: A tidy summary of each customer, prepared specifically for the AI models.
entities.why: If these numbers are wrong, the AI is confidently wrong.

layers.name: Pipelines
layers.plain_blurb: Scheduled jobs that rebuild the tables above on a timer.

entities.name: build_fct_orders
entities.description: Airflow task materialising fct_orders each morning.
entities.plain_description: Runs every morning to rebuild the orders table.
entities.why: If it fails, today's revenue numbers are yesterday's.

entities.name: build_customer_features
entities.description: Airflow task refreshing the ML feature table hourly.
entities.plain_description: Keeps the AI's input numbers up to date.
entities.why: If it stalls, the AI is working from stale information.

entities.name: train_churn_predictor
entities.description: Weekly retraining run for the production churn model.
entities.plain_description: Teaches the cancellation-predictor using the latest data.
entities.why: A bad retrain quietly changes every prediction that follows.

entities.name: train_ltv_regressor
entities.description: Ad-hoc training run for the staging LTV regressor.
entities.plain_description: Retrains the not-yet-live customer value model.
entities.why: Low stakes for now — this model isn't in use.

layers.name: Consumers
layers.plain_blurb: The dashboards people read and the AI models making live decisions.

entities.name: Executive Revenue Overview
entities.description: Board-level revenue reporting. Reviewed weekly by the exec team.
entities.plain_description: The chart the executive team looks at every week.
entities.why: Wrong numbers here get repeated in meetings and decisions.

entities.name: Churn Monitoring
entities.description: Tracks churn model scores against actual churn.
entities.plain_description: Tracks how well the AI is predicting who leaves.
entities.why: How anyone would notice the AI has gone wrong.

entities.name: Finance Month-End Close
entities.description: Used by Finance to close the books each month. Numbers here are reported externally, so a silent change upstream is expensive.
entities.plain_description: What Finance uses to close the books each month.
entities.why: These numbers get reported outside the company. Errors are expensive.

entities.name: churn_predictor
entities.plain_name: AI that predicts who will cancel
entities.description: Production churn model, v3. Scores every active customer nightly; output drives the retention discount campaign.
entities.plain_description: Scores every customer each night for how likely they are to leave.
entities.why: Live in production — it decides who gets a retention discount, so bad scores cost real money.

entities.name: ltv_regressor
entities.description: Staging LTV regressor, not yet serving traffic.
entities.plain_description: Estimates what a customer will be worth in future.
entities.why: Still being tested, not yet making decisions.

graph.stakes: Someone renames one column in the payments table. Four steps later, the AI that decides which customers get a discount starts making bad calls — and nothing anywhere says the two are connected.

blast_cold.question: We want to rename raw.stripe.charges.amount_cents to amount_minor_units and change its type from NUMBER to VARCHAR to support zero-decimal currencies. What breaks?

stages.name: resolve
stages.detail: named directly in the question: raw.stripe.charges

blast_cold.answer: raw.stripe.charges feeds churn_predictor (MLMODEL), 4 hops downstream. Changing raw.stripe.charges puts 12 downstream assets at risk, including critical ones like churn_predictor and ltv_regressor. Teams analytics_eng, bi_team, finance_systems, and ml_platform must be consulted to assess potential impact on Executive Revenue Overview, Finance Month-End Close, and other key reports.

cause.question: The churn_predictor model started scoring almost every customer as high-risk overnight. Nothing was deployed to the model itself. What upstream is most likely responsible?

stages.name: resolve
stages.detail: named directly in the question: churn_predictor

cause.answer: churn_predictor incident: train_churn_predictor is the leading upstream candidate. The leading candidate is train_churn_predictor, which is a potential cause but not confirmed. To investigate, check the train_churn_predictor job logs first for any errors or failures that may have triggered the issue on churn_predictor.
